transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... my regular doctor thought I should come in because she says I’ve gotten too thin. I guess I can see what she means, in a practical sort of way—like my work pants, the ones I wear when I’m cleaning, they’re hanging loose on me now, and I keep having to pull them up. They didn’t used to fit like that.

But it’s confusing, because even though I hear her saying it like it’s a problem, part of me still feels... I don’t know, relieved, I guess, when I step on the scale and the number is lower. Like I know I’m supposed to be concerned, but there’s this other feeling that says lower is better. That’s mostly what brings me in, I think—my doctor being worried, and me not being quite able to feel worried in the same way.
Can you tell me about your eating habits lately—have you been trying to eat less or avoid certain foods because you’re worried about gaining weight?

Yes... I suppose I have been eating less. I don’t always think of it that way while I’m doing it, because I’m still around food, you know? I still cook dinner. I make proper plates for my husband and for my mother-in-law, and I’ll stand there making sure they have enough—meat or whatever we’re having, potatoes, vegetables, the whole thing.

But then when it’s time for me to sit down, it’s like something changes in my head. I’ll look at the plate and think, well, I don’t really need all that. I’ll tell myself coffee is fine, or I’ll just have some vegetables, or maybe half a piece of toast if I feel like I should have something. And at the time it seems reasonable to me, like I’m just being careful or I’m not that hungry, but I guess if I’m honest, there is that worry underneath about eating too much and then gaining weight.
Can you tell me if you have been intentionally trying to keep your weight low or avoid gaining any weight, even if it means eating very little or skipping meals?

Yes… I think I have. It feels strange saying it that plainly, because in my head I call it other things, like “being careful” or “not overdoing it,” but yes, I do try very hard not to let my weight go up.

If I eat something that feels heavier to me—like biscuits, or pasta, something like that—I can’t just eat it and move on. I spend the rest of the day thinking about it. I’ll be cleaning or folding laundry or whatever I’m doing, and my mind keeps going back to, “That was too much,” or “Is it going to show on me?” I’ll check myself, like looking at my stomach or how my waistband feels, even if I know that probably doesn’t make sense right away.

And then I start thinking I need to make up for it somehow. Not necessarily in some dramatic way, but I’ll think, “Well, then I shouldn’t have much later,” or “I’ll just stick to coffee,” or I’ll try to keep things very small. It’s like I can’t relax after eating those foods. I get scared it’s going to change my body, even from one meal, and then I spend hours trying to undo it in my head.
